fact_text: The Thar Block II coal mine extracts about 7.6 million tonnes of coal a year, according to the video, with capacity expected to reach 11.2 million tonnes by 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: SECMC said Thar Block II produces about 7 million tonnes of coal a year, all used for power generation, up from an original start of about 3.5 million tonnes a year.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: Three power plants sit at the Thar mine mouth and together generate about 1,320 MW from the mine's coal, which the video says supplies power to about 3 million households.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: Existing power plants are designed for imported coal, whose calorific value differs from Thar coal, so they need modification and investment before full use of Thar coal.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: Without plant modification, Thar coal can be blended at about 15-20% with imported coal, and trial runs are being carried out at several power plants.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: A recent policy change lets Thar coal be used beyond power generation, including by the cement and textile sectors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: As of 13 Nov 2025, the cement sector depends fully on imported coal and is trial-testing Thar coal, with blending possible before plant modification, according to the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: The video says cheaper Thar coal in cement could lower cement prices, benefiting the wider economy, although this is the presenter's reasoning rather than a measured result.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: A fertiliser company is at an advanced stage of plans to build a plant at Thar that would turn coal into gas and then into fertiliser, as domestic gas reserves decline, per the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: SECMC monitors slope failure, the mine's main landslide risk, with radar-based displacement monitoring, and uses cameras and electric haul trucks to cut fuel use.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: SECMC received an excellence award from the World Digital Forum in four categories: innovation, sustainability, environment and expansion, and says it is the first Pakistani mining company to win such an award.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: SECMC says it aims to secure Pakistan's energy supply through the Thar project and that its designs are done by Pakistani engineers using its own software.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: The video's reasoning is that a fuel cost gap of about three times between Thar and imported coal makes Thar-based power much cheaper, while noting that plant modification needs further investment.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: Pakistan's total coal reserve is about 175 billion tonnes, which the speaker said holds more energy than the oil that Iran and Saudi Arabia have.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: Pakistan's electricity requirement is about 35,000 MW in summer, the speaker said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: Pakistan's electricity requirement is about 18,000 MW in winter, the speaker said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: The Thar coal mine plans to expand output to 7 to 11.5 million tonnes a year by 2026, the speaker said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)

fact_text: A rail link of about 100 km to the Thar coal area is being laid, with completion expected in 2026, the speaker said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Thar Coal: How Pakistan’s Cheapest Energy Source Is Powering the Future | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-11-13)
